title: The Educated Barbarian: Book of Five Rings analysis (part. 7)
summary: NH continues his reading of Musashi's Book of Five Rings, applying passages on the voice, the 'mountain-sea' change, 'rat's head ox's neck', letting go of the hilt and the body of a rock to lifting and life. He covers shouting during sets, changing a failing method after a second try, independence from equipment, and the link between a strong body and a strong mind.
claims: The literature review series moves to a weekly Tuesday slot so he can reach the Hagakure, stoicism and Nietzsche sooner
The tone and pitch of a voice reveal a person's state of mind, confidence or lying, and we decide whom to trust partly on it
Training against the elements, such as fighting waves or standing under a cold waterfall, strengthens body and mind
Shouting in the middle of a tough set re-invigorates you and makes the rest easier, while a timid half-shout can psych you out
Musashi's three shouts map onto lifting as shouting before the set, on each rep and after; commercial gyms will kick you out but a home gym allows it
Shouting costs mental stamina and spikes adrenaline, which can leave you depleted like too much coffee, so use it only when necessary
Mountain-sea spirit applied to lifting: a method that caused a plateau or injury once will likely do it again; give it a second try, but if it fails again change it
For a serious lifter who understands recovery, a failing program is most likely the methodology's fault (rep ranges, volume, intensity) rather than the lifter's
Do not fall into constantly rotating methods without progress; trying something twice before abandoning it strikes the balance
Rat's head, ox's neck: when absorbed in small details, step back to the big picture and vice versa; small and big are subjective framings
Equipment does not hold the power to build you: owning a squat rack does not guarantee leg development and lacking one does not prevent it; the drive is internal
Minimalism over materialism: things you own should be tools, not extensions of your spirit, or they end up owning you
Lowering body fat and building dense muscle, plus strong legs and core, make the body harder and more stable, closer to Musashi's 'body of a rock'
A strong body goes hand in hand with a strong mind and vice versa; he took this idea from Musashi
'You will not be moved' means you decide whether to be moved and cannot be emotionally manipulated, not that you are inflexible
After 10 years of lifting it took him a long time to conceptualize the principles he applied daily
People who absorb second-hand knowledge before gaining practical experience become smug and arrogant; practice should come first, then sharing
First experiences shape people permanently, so early bad influences are very hard to undo
Try things and make your own mistakes; studying a thousand books to avoid all mistakes removes training from the center of your life
